dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.subtitle: What came in this morning, and how much of it survived.
dashboard.followUpsHint: Recorded by hand, on the pipeline board
dashboard.measuredBaseline: Everything in the archive, not one run
dashboard.repeats: {count, plural, one {# listing appeared in two documents} other {# listings appeared in two documents}}
dashboard.noRepeats: Every extracted offer was a new row
dashboard.noRunYetHint: Run ingest from the header. It reads every enabled source once and reports what each document gave up.
dashboard.hardFilterNote: Six stages, in the order they run. Each one states what it removed; the rail narrows to what is left.
dashboard.nothingFiltered: Nothing has been filtered yet. Run ingest, and this counts the archive.
dashboard.recordedRun: Recorded by the pipeline, finished {when}. Nothing has been run from this browser.
dashboard.recordedRunLimits: A recorded run is counted per source. Which document came up short is known only while the run is being watched.
dashboard.mismatch: {count, plural, one {# document extracted fewer offers than it announced} other {# documents extracted fewer offers than they announced}}. A selector that stopped matching looks exactly like a quiet market.
dashboard.archivedNote: {count, plural, one {# offer is} other {# offers are}} archived and outside these numbers.

shortlist.title: Shortlist
shortlist.subtitle: What cleared the hard filter, with the reason it scored what it scored.
shortlist.noMatchHint: Clear them to see the whole shortlist again.
shortlist.emptyHint: Ingest reads the sources and the hard filter thins them out. Run it from the header to fill this list.
shortlist.emptyArchiveHint: Offers leave the working list when they age past the freshness window, or when you take them off it yourself.

offer.notScored: Not scored. The pipeline ran without a language model, so this is the hard filter's answer only.
offer.alsoOn: {count, plural, one {also on # more} other {also on # more}}

detail.fromSource: From the source document. The original ad was not fetched.
detail.whyScored: Why it scored what it scored
detail.notScored: Not scored. Without a language model the pipeline still produces this shortlist, only unranked.
detail.packageNote: The package is a folder on disk: cover letter, the fixed CV for the ad's language, and the matching reference projects. Nothing is sent from here.
detail.packageOnDisk: The folder is on the machine that ran the pipeline. The download bundles it as a zip; nothing is sent from here.
detail.noPackageYet: A package is built for everything above the shortlist threshold. This offer has none yet.
detail.notFoundHint: It may have been superseded by a newer run. Go back to the shortlist and pick it there.
detail.archivedByAge: It aged past the freshness window.

application.title: Where this stands
application.note: The mail goes out from your own client, so nothing here is observed — every value is what you say happened. No transition is refused, and a wrong one can be corrected.

pipeline.title: Pipeline
pipeline.subtitle: The half of the loop the tool cannot see. Nothing is sent from here, so everything here is recorded by hand.
pipeline.emptyHint: An application opens when its package is built. Run ingest, and everything above the shortlist threshold arrives in Prepared.

review.title: Review
review.subtitle: An upload becomes an offer only once somebody has seen what was read from it.
review.drop: Drop a Markdown file here, or choose one
review.dropHint: YAML frontmatter carries the fields, the body is the description. A file without it still works; you fill the fields in here.
review.noFrontmatter: No frontmatter in this file, so nothing could be read from it deterministically. Fill the fields in below; the text is on the right.
review.duplicate: Already in the pipeline as “{title}”. Confirming adds a second listing, which deduplication collapses into one entry naming both sources.
review.confirmNote: Confirming writes these fields back into the file and moves it where the source reads.
review.emptyHint: Drop a Markdown file above. It lands in the inbox unread, and enters the pipeline on the next run once you confirm it.
review.summary: {waiting, plural, one {# file waiting for review} other {# files waiting for review}}.
review.summaryWithDuplicates: {waiting, plural, one {# file waiting for review} other {# files waiting for review}}, {duplicates, plural, one {# already in the pipeline} other {# already in the pipeline}}.

sources.title: Sources
sources.subtitle: Where offers come from, how much each one yields, and which configuration layer defined it.
sources.emptyHint: Every source is a block in sources.yaml. Without an external file the shipped defaults apply, and those are all switched off except the manual inbox.
sources.note: Adding a source is a YAML block in sources.yaml, not a deploy. The file is hot-reloaded, so this screen reads and does not edit.

rules.title: Rules
rules.subtitle: The hard filter, the scoring weights and the thresholds behind every number on the shortlist.
rules.knockoutsNote: These run deterministically and for free, before any model call. Without a language model the tool still works, only weaker.
rules.readOnly: Read-only. The rules come from matching-rules.yaml and there is no write endpoint yet, so editing here would only lie about what was saved.
rules.archiveAfter: An offer leaves the working list once the ad is more than {days} days old. It stays readable and can be put back by hand.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.subtitle: What the market is doing, and what the rules are doing to it.
analytics.tilePerWeekHint: Averaged over the span, not over the busy days
analytics.tileResponseHint: Of the applications you recorded as sent
analytics.intakeCaption: Offers per bucket, with how many cleared the filter and how many were the same project twice.
analytics.emptyHint: Run ingest from the header. One pass is enough for the first bar; a few days make it a trend.
analytics.emptyAxisHint: No offer states a publication date yet. Switch to Arrived, which every offer carries.
analytics.portalsNote: What each portal published, with the projects that cleared the filter marked inside the bar. A listing another portal carried first still counts as published.
analytics.tagsNote: The categories the source files its offers under — not skills read out of the advert.
analytics.locationsNote: As each advert wrote it, unnormalised. “Remote und Nürnberg” and “Nürnberg” are two rows.
analytics.reach: Decided rather than guessed: {outOfReach} out of reach, {abroad} abroad, {remoteShare} below the remote share.
analytics.scoresNote: Where the two thresholds cut the archive. The question is whether the mass sits just under a line somebody chose.
analytics.scoresCaption: How many offers fall in each ten-point band.
analytics.unscored: {count, plural, one {# offer was left unscored} other {# offers were left unscored}} — the deterministic reasons were written and the total withheld.
analytics.applicationsCaption: How many applications stand in each state.
analytics.applicationsEmpty: No application has been opened yet. One opens when a package is built.
analytics.medianDays: median {days} days to the first answer
analytics.backdated: {count, plural, one {# application has a reply recorded before it was sent} other {# applications have a reply recorded before they were sent}}, and is left out of the median.
analytics.stageMixCaption: Offers removed per week and stage, under today's rules.
analytics.recomputedNote: The filter re-judges every offer on every run and overwrites the verdict. These bars are today's rules applied to the offers that arrived in each week — not what the rules did at the time.
analytics.scalesOne: One scale in the archive: ruleset {ruleset}, model {model}. Every score above is comparable to every other.
analytics.scalesMixed: {count} different scales in the archive. Scores produced under different rulesets or judges are not comparable, so nothing here should be read as a trend.
analytics.scalesNone: Nothing has been scored, so there is no scale to state.
analytics.runsNote: Written down while it was still true. Every other number on this page is read off the archive as it stands now; these were recorded before the next run overwrote them.
analytics.runsCaption: One row per run: what it extracted, what cleared the filter, what reached the shortlist, and under which scale.
analytics.runsEmpty: No run has been recorded yet. The next one will be, and this table starts from there — it cannot be filled in backwards.
analytics.historySince: Run history starts on {date}. Anything before that was overwritten before this table existed.
analytics.axisExcluded: {undated} state no date and {outOfRange} are older than the window, so neither is on this axis.

axisNote.published: The date each advert states, over the last 90 days. What the market published, as far as it says so.
axisNote.received: The day the mail carrying the offer arrived. The only one of the three that measures the market's tempo rather than yours.
axisNote.ingested: The day this application wrote the row. A measurement, but it also counts how often you ran the tool — and every row moves if the database is refilled.

analytics.axisWithoutMail: {count} did not come in the post and are not on this axis.
analytics.tilePerWeekTooShort: Not yet: the series covers less than a week, and a weekly rate from it would be a guess

error.funnelLoad: The filter counts did not load.
error.queueLoad: The review queue did not load.
error.ingestRun: The ingest run did not answer.
error.lastRun: The last run could not be read.
error.rescore: The offer was not scored again.
error.scoringModelsLoad: The scoring models did not load.
error.archive: The archive could not be changed.
